title: Divide Array Into Arrays With Max Difference
statement:
The length `n` of `nums` is a multiple of 3, and `k` is a positive integer. Split all of `nums` into `n / 3` groups of exactly three elements, using each position exactly once, so that inside every group the largest value minus the smallest value is at most `k`.

Return the groups as a 2D array. If no such split exists, return an empty array. When several splits work, any one is accepted, with the groups and the values inside each group in any order.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every way to cut the array into triples explodes quickly. Sorting removes the guesswork: the smallest value has to sit in some group, and the cheapest partners it can take are the next two smallest values, because any other choice only makes that group's spread larger and leaves bigger values for the rest. Repeating the argument, the sorted array split into consecutive triples is the best possible split. If even one of those triples is too wide, no split works.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in ascending order.
2. Walk `i` over the start of each consecutive triple: `0, 3, 6, ...`.
3. In sorted order the spread of a triple is its last value minus its first. If `nums[i + 2] - nums[i]` exceeds `k`, return `[]`.
4. Otherwise append the triple to `groups`.
5. After the loop every triple fits, so return `groups`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1,3,4,8,7,9,3,5,1]`, `k = 2`. Sorted it becomes `[1,1,3,3,4,5,7,8,9]`.

- `i = 0`: triple `[1,1,3]`, spread `3 - 1 = 2`, which is not above 2, so keep it.
- `i = 3`: triple `[3,4,5]`, spread 2, keep it.
- `i = 6`: triple `[7,8,9]`, spread 2, keep it.

The answer is `[[1,1,3],[3,4,5],[7,8,9]]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n), dominated by the sort; the scan is linear.
- Space: O(n) for the returned groups (O(log n) extra for the sort).

## Pitfalls

- Checking only neighbouring pairs is not enough: the rule covers the first and third value of a group, so compare `nums[i + 2]` with `nums[i]`.
- The limit is inclusive: a spread exactly equal to `k` is allowed.
- Return an empty array as soon as one triple fails; partial groups are not an answer.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `groups` | the triples built so far |
| `i` | index of the first value of the current triple in sorted `nums` |
| `k` | the largest spread a group may have |

narration.2: Sort the values so that each group can be taken from neighbouring positions.
narration.5: Step through the sorted array three values at a time.
narration.6: In sorted order the widest pair of a triple is its first and last value; is that gap bigger than k?
narration.7: Then no split can work, so return an empty array.
narration.9: The triple fits, so add it to the answer.
narration.11: Every consecutive triple fits; return them all.
